sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page douz1234 (Douz Sign Language) and reference records 683413 (Nefaa 2023) and 666532 (Pizzuto 2001)
sources.note: No descriptive references at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); only two subclassification notes: Pizzuto 2001 ('no historical connection to another sign language documented') and Nefaa 2023 (subsumes Douz SL under Tunisian Sign; LSF cognate rate in the low 30% range).

sources.citation: Nefaa, Aymen. 2023. Approche éducative trilingue biculturelle pour les enfants sourds en Tunisie : attitudes et applicabilité. Doctoral thesis, Sciences du langage, Aix-Marseille Université, NNT 2023AIXM0388. 355 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Education / language-attitude study; pp. 103-104 summarise Fusellier-Souza 2004: 65 on Douz as a village-sign-language setting (school founded 1982, endogamous marriages, high hereditary deafness); an interviewee (p. 337) says sign language 'est une langue existante à Douz, et tout le monde l'utilise dans la rue'. No grammatical or phonological description.

sources.citation: Nefaa, Aymen. 2023. Genetic relatedness of Tunisian Sign Language and French Sign Language. Frontiers in Communication 8:1201148, pp. 1-11. doi:10.3389/fcomm.2023.1201148
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical comparison of LST (signers from Tunis, Nabeul and Douz/Kebili) with LSF; Douz appears only as a sampling site (abstract p. 1) and Kebili is flagged (p. 7) as a setting where a Zeshan & de Vos 'Village Sign Language' could emerge; cognate rate with LSF 33% for Kebili (p. 8). Only phonological content is the four sign parameters (handshape, movement, location, orientation) used for cognate matching. No prosody, no stress.

sources.citation: Fusellier-Souza, Ivani. 2004. Sémiogenèse des langues des signes. Étude de langues des signes émergentes (LSE) pratiquées par des sourds brésiliens. Doctoral thesis, Université Paris 8 (NNT 2004PA082477), vol. 1, 416 pp. HAL tel-01701214.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or prosody for Douz. Section 4.3.2 'Emergence institutionnelle d'une LS pratiquée à Douz (Tunisie)', pp. 65-66: a school founded in Douz in 1982 (Belarbi 1995) grouped ~100 deaf children/adolescents (2-20 yrs) who had previously lived isolated in hearing families in villages around Douz; over ~20 years they developed their own gestural linguistic system; an Italian CNR project (Pizzuto 2001) was launched in 2001 to analyse it, results 'futurs'. HAL file is behind an Anubis bot-check; obtained from the the Internet Archive snapshot of the HAL file (2024-09-11).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page tuni1249 (Tunisian Sign Language, ISO tse)
sources.note: Only classification/endangerment references (Corazza 1993; Boyes Braem & Rathmann 2010; Quer et al. 2010; Kamei 2004; Nefaa 2023; Ethnologue 2025); no grammar or phonology of LST listed.
